newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah chief warns of Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah chief warns of Israeli blitz on Lebanon.

text.p: The leader of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah group was quoted on Monday as saying Israel might launch a wide-scale attack against Moslem guerrillas and Syrian troops in Lebanon.

Shiekh Hassan Nasrallah, secretary-general of the Shi'ite Moslem group, said the aim of such a military campaign would be to impose Israel's conditions for the resumption of the suspended peace talks with Beirut and Damascus.

"Hoping to force Lebanon and Syria back to negotiations under its conditions, Israel might resort to a wide-scale aggression if it proves to be the only and best means (to reach the goal)," Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah, secretary-general of the pro-Iranian group, told as-Safir newspaper in an interview.
He said Israel's "obstinacy in peace talks...and the addition of hundreds of millions of dollars to the Israeli defence budget indicate that everything in Israel is going in the direction of a war".

Nasrallah said the possible military operation would be larger than an April 1996 Israeli blitz on Lebanon but smaller than the 1982 all-out Israeli invasion. Last April, Israel killed more than 200 people in air, sea and land bombardment.

The Shi'ite Moslem cleric said a possible scenario for an Israeli blitz would include air raids on Syrian troops in Lebanon, on Hizbollah and even on the Lebanese army "in an attempt to dismantle it".
Syria has 35,000 troops deployed across two-thirds of Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.
Nasrallah, however, warned that such an Israeli attack "could open the door for a regional war".

"Israel will be taking a risk (by hitting Syrian targets in Lebanon) because it will not be able to predict the Syrian reaction to such attack aimed at its direct military presence on the Lebanese platform," he said.

Asked to comment on growing expectations of a possible Israeli strike on Syria, Nasrallah said: "A war on Syria inside Syria does not change the equation. It changes the region, because such a move might blow up the whole peace process".

Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war to oust Israeli troops from a 15-km (nine miles) south Lebanon occupation zone. In 1996, Hizbollah guerrillas killed 27 Israeli soldiers inside the buffer zone.

Peace talks between Lebanon and Israel -- launched in 1991 -- have been suspended for nearly three years. Talks between Syria and Israel, stalled over withdrawal from the Israeli occupied Golan Heights and the nature of future ties, have been suspended for 11 months.
